packageRoles.full: Control package: used for ALL performance measurement (plus the backend comparison).
packageRoles.slim: Deployment package: used ONLY for APK size and memory. No performance comparison is made between the two packages.

primary.protocol: Predefined: control package, 3 x 60 s continuous camera, app force-stopped between runs and restarted only after HAL SKIN <= 46 C, first 20 processed frames excluded.
primary.note: These three runs ARE the reported deployment performance result. Session-level only; frames are never pooled across sessions.

diagnostics.purpose: Post-hoc investigation of why the slim sessions were slower. NOT part of the predefined protocol; these numbers are not performance results.
diagnostics.decisiveResult: The full-build recheck is the same build as primary run 1, with pre-timing SKIN only 0.20 C higher, yet measured 21.5% slower (242.34 -> 294.41 ms) about 16 minutes later.
conclusions: The build effect and the session drift are confounded; NO equivalence conclusion is drawn between the two packages.
It also cannot be claimed that the slowdown was caused by the deployment package. The evidence supports only: no evidence that it was caused by that build difference.
Across all six sessions the pre-timing SKIN range is 2.3 C while the session-mean range is 1.29x, so the drift is not explained by the temperature readings available here.
No causal attribution is made (no CPU frequency, scheduler state, power policy or throttling events were recorded).
The deployment package is used for APK size and memory only; it takes part in no FPS or latency comparison.

backToBackContrast.note: Superseded runs with no reset between them. Methodological contrast only, NOT results.

evidence: B.5.1 fixed-frame replay: 1.45-1.76x between two sessions, same device and protocol.
This protocol: 1.22x (+21.5%, 242.34 -> 294.41 ms) between two sessions of the SAME build, about 16 min apart, pre-timing SKIN differing by 0.20 C.
sessionDependence.statement: Absolute latency is strongly session-dependent and the available device-state readings do not establish that two sessions ran under equivalent conditions. Cause undetermined. Absolute latency is reported as ranges only, structural conclusions use within-session paired ratios, and no causal attribution is made. This bounds the deployment section as preliminary on-device deployment validation, not a strict mobile performance benchmark.
sessionDependence.resetCaveat: The reset reduces the spread between adjacent runs (6% vs 42% back to back) but does not make the measurement repeatable: the same build re-run later at a similar starting SKIN was clearly slower. A single skin-temperature reset does not guarantee comparable performance state across periods.
